findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:47 — optimized_pagination=true` is a plain unauthenticated-scope query parameter read directly off `request.GET` with no additional validation; combined with the `has_global_access` gate this makes the entire "advanced"/negative-offset code path opt-in and trivially toggled by any client who satisfies (or believes they satisfy) that permission check, increasing the attack surface for the P0 offset issue above.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:33 — Removing the start/end/statsPeriod filter serializer fields and the datetime__range queryset filter drops the only query-narrowing predicate, so every audit log listing now scans the full unfiltered table/index instead of a bounded date range.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:156 — queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` allows negative offsets to reach the Django ORM slice, but Django QuerySets explicitly disallow negative indexing/slicing and raise an error rather than "handling boundary conditions automatically" as the comment claims — this is not a performance optimization but a broken code path that will throw on any negative-offset cursor.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:153 — Even if negative slicing worked, `queryset[negative:stop]` on an unindexed/unsliced-from-start queryset forces Django to evaluate the full ordered queryset (or a large prefix of it) to resolve a negative start, which is equivalent to a full table scan for large audit log tables — the opposite of the intended "avoid full dataset scanning" goal.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:97 — OptimizedCursorPaginator` duplicates almost all of `BasePaginator.get_result` but adds no actual query optimization (no new indexing hints, no LIMIT/OFFSET reduction) other than the broken negative-offset path, so for the non-negative-offset case it performs identically to `DateTimePaginator`/`BasePaginator` while adding overhead and risk with no measured benefit.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:47 — The new `optimized_pagination=true` path is user-controlled via query param and only gated by a superuser/global-access check computed per request; combined with the broken negative-offset handling, an authorized admin can trigger unbounded/erroring queries against the audit log table simply by passing a negative-offset cursor.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — Advanced pagination is gated by `request.user.is_superuser` directly instead of Sentry's `is_active_superuser()` helper, so a stale/impersonated superuser flag without an active elevated session can unlock the advanced-features path.

goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:47 — optimized_pagination=true` is a plain unauthenticated-scope query parameter read directly off `request.GET` with no additional validation; combined with the `has_global_access` gate this makes the entire "advanced"/negative-offset code path opt-in and trivially toggled by any client who satisfies (or believes they satisfy) that permission check, increasing the attack surface for the P0 offset issue above.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a client-controlled opt-in switch: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` in `organization_auditlogs.py`, and when combined with `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, any authorized caller can toggle the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` path (and thus `enable_advanced_features=True`). There is no additional validation or server-side feature flagging beyond that boolean GET param and permission gate. However, this is more of an architectural/attack-surface concern than a directly verifiable defect from the diff alone (and the claim it is “unauthenticated-scope” can’t be confirmed from the shown changes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:33 — Removing the start/end/statsPeriod filter serializer fields and the datetime__range queryset filter drops the only query-narrowing predicate, so every audit log listing now scans the full unfiltered table/index instead of a bounded date range.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes pagination behavior in `organization_auditlogs.py` (switching between `DateTimePaginator` and a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` based on query param and permissions) and adds/adjusts paginator logic to handle offsets. It does not show removal of any start/end/statsPeriod serializer fields or removal of a `datetime__range` filter. The existing queryset filtering code shown still applies event-based filtering; there is no evidence in this diff that date-range narrowing was removed or that the listing now scans an unfiltered table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:153 — Even if negative slicing worked, `queryset[negative:stop]` on an unindexed/unsliced-from-start queryset forces Django to evaluate the full ordered queryset (or a large prefix of it) to resolve a negative start, which is equivalent to a full table scan for large audit log tables — the opposite of the intended "avoid full dataset scanning" goal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces/permits negative offsets for queryset slicing (e.g., `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, and also `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`), with comments claiming it avoids full dataset scanning. Whether Django resolves negative slicing by scanning a large prefix isn’t verifiable from the diff alone, but the change clearly rests on an assumption about ORM behavior/performance that may be wrong and could negate the intended optimization on large audit-log querysets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:97 — OptimizedCursorPaginator` duplicates almost all of `BasePaginator.get_result` but adds no actual query optimization (no new indexing hints, no LIMIT/OFFSET reduction) other than the broken negative-offset path, so for the non-negative-offset case it performs identically to `DateTimePaginator`/`BasePaginator` while adding overhead and risk with no measured benefit.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` adds an “advanced” branch that explicitly allows a negative `start_offset` (`start_offset = cursor.offset` when `cursor.offset < 0`) and then slices the Django queryset with that negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indexes and will raise at runtime, so enabling `optimized_pagination=true` for an admin can break pagination. The rest of the method largely mirrors the existing `BasePaginator.get_result` logic, so the primary functional change is this risky negative-offset path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:47 — The new `optimized_pagination=true` path is user-controlled via query param and only gated by a superuser/global-access check computed per request; combined with the broken negative-offset handling, an authorized admin can trigger unbounded/erroring queries against the audit log table simply by passing a negative-offset cursor.

adjudication.rationale: The new `optimized_pagination=true` branch is indeed request-controlled (org_auditlogs.py) and, when enabled for admins, passes `enable_advanced_features=True` into the newly added `OptimizedCursorPaginator`. That paginator explicitly allows negative offsets (`if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0: start_offset = cursor.offset; results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`). Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indexes, so a crafted cursor with a negative `offset` can trigger exceptions/500s in this path. The diff also updates another paginator path to preserve negative offsets for `cursor.is_prev` (`start_offset = ... else offset`), reinforcing the same risk. The “unbounded” aspect isn’t directly shown, but “erroring queries” via negative offsets is a real defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — Advanced pagination is gated by `request.user.is_superuser` directly instead of Sentry's `is_active_superuser()` helper, so a stale/impersonated superuser flag without an active elevated session can unlock the advanced-features path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a privileged code path gated by `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` (organization_auditlogs.py). This directly checks the `is_superuser` flag to enable `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`. While the diff doesn’t prove Sentry must use `is_active_superuser()` here, it does show a new admin-only feature gate implemented via a raw superuser boolean rather than a centralized/stronger helper, which is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern for consistency and intended authorization semantics.
